extracted.intended_audience: neuroscientists and mathematicians interested in mathematical aesthetics / rubric designers for math aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Designing or applying a rubric to rate the aesthetic beauty of mathematical formulae/theorems (not full proofs), grounded in empirical neuroaesthetic findings from Zeki et al. The rubric should operationalize perceptual features that correlate with high beauty ratings and neural activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: mOFC activation (neural correlate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical beauty activates field A1 of the medial orbito-frontal cortex (mOFC) — the same region activated by visual and musical beauty (Zeki et al.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neural activation (mOFC) as an empirical validation metric where available (e.g., fMRI studies). This supports treating mathematical beauty as a perceptual/neural phenomenon rather than purely idiosyncratic preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric scaling with rated beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Activation in mOFC scales parametrically with rated beauty (more beautiful → more activation), suggesting beauty judgments are continuous, not categorical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat beauty as a graded/continuous score in the rubric (allowing partial credit and parametric scaling) rather than only binary beautiful/ugly labels; consider collecting numeric ratings rather than only categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus / high inter-rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: High inter-rater agreement on which formulae are most beautiful, despite individual differences elsewhere — implying shared features within the mathematical community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful rubric should emphasize features that produce agreement across knowledgeable raters; include procedures to measure inter-rater reliability and prioritize features that correlate with consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness / conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Compactness: short statement — many highly rated formulae are brief and compact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward conciseness and symbolic compression in formula presentation. Penalize verbose or expanded expressions when a much shorter equivalent exists; prefer minimal, canonical forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-domain unification (connection of disparate domains)
rubrics_metrics.description: Connection of disparate domains: beautiful formulae often link constants or concepts from different areas (e.g., Euler's identity linking e, i, π, 1, 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward evident unifying power across mathematical subfields—formulas that reveal deep relationships between previously separate concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitability / necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Inevitability: the result feels necessary, not contingent — a sense that the relationship must be so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score higher those formulae that convey a sense of inevitability or naturalness; de-emphasize constructions that feel forced or arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprising compression: a deep relation expressed in minimal symbols — the combination of unexpectedness and compactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward formulae that compress surprising or counterintuitive facts into a concise expression; capture both novelty/surprise and economy of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generativity / theory-building potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative: each is a starting point for a large theory; beautiful formulae often open avenues for broad mathematical development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor results that seed further work or unify into a broader conceptual framework, not isolated gimmicks or one-off curiosities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for expanded or reducible forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark down expanded forms of expressions reducible to simpler ones — even if mathematically equivalent; expanded/combinatorial expansions were often judged ugly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly penalize non-canonical expanded presentations when a simpler equivalent exists; encourage presenting results in their most compressed, conceptually clear form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of organizing structure (negative feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ugly formulae were typically long combinatorial expansions with no organizing structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Downweight long, structureless expressions; reward evident structure, pattern, or principled organization that aids comprehension and aesthetic appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitrary-looking coefficients / opaque parameters (negative feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Series identities with arbitrary-looking coefficients were often rated ugly — coefficients or parameters that look ad hoc reduce aesthetic appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalize formulas whose constants or coefficients appear arbitrary or lack clear conceptual origin; reward those with meaningful, natural constants or parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation: criteria apply to formulae, not necessarily proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological caveat: the study used formulae (theorems), not full proofs. The neuroaesthetic basis of proof beauty (which involves reading/following) may engage additional circuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing rubrics, distinguish between aesthetic criteria for static formulae/theorems and those for proofs; do not assume these formula-based criteria fully capture the aesthetics of proofs (consider temporality, readability, explanatory clarity for proofs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric design principle: reward features common to high-rated formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: A rubric for 'mathematical beauty' should reward the features common to the high-rated formulae: compression, cross-domain unification, inevitability, generativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the empirically-identified feature set as the core of any aesthetic rubric; construct explicit sub-scores for compression, unification, necessity, and generativity and combine them (possibly parametrically) to produce an overall beauty score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-evidence: beauty is shared / neurally real (implication for objectivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical beauty is not subjective in the strong sense: it is shared, parametric, and neurally real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat aesthetic evaluation as partly objective/communal for expert communities; design rubrics that aim for reproducibility across expert raters and that can be validated empirically (ratings, inter-rater reliability, and where possible neural correlates).
